> Curated papers, systems, and datasets for Text-to-SQL that can recognize ambiguity, ask useful questions, and decline unsupported requests.

Natural-language questions do not always determine one SQL query, and a database cannot answer every request. This collection focuses on how NL2SQL agents detect these situations, resolve them through interaction or additional evidence, and evaluate when to answer or abstain.

[**Explore the interactive catalog →**](https://duyvuleo.github.io/awesome-reliable-text-to-sql/) · [Browse papers](papers/README.md) · [Compare benchmarks](docs/benchmark-matrix.md) · [Try the examples](examples/README.md) · [Contribute](CONTRIBUTING.md)

Updated **2026-11-13**. Each paper includes a concise summary, publication status, public sources, and a verification date. Core work and adjacent methods are marked separately. Resource counts include clearly labeled benchmark designs whose artifacts are not yet verified released.

[**Read the detailed paper notes →**](papers/reading-notes.md) for methods, evaluation conditions, findings, limitations and checks against the original text. The index records completed readings and remaining access gaps.

## Scope

We include work that directly studies ambiguity, underspecification, answerability, clarification, or abstention in natural-language querying of relational databases. We also include selected verification, uncertainty, and contextual-grounding methods when their relevance to those problems is explicit. Generic SQL-generation systems and broad agent frameworks belong in the related collections unless they provide a concrete capability relevant to this scope.

An ambiguous request, an unsupported request, a model error, and a valid query returning no rows are different cases. Likewise, a publication, an announced repository, released artifacts, and independently reproduced results are different kinds of evidence. The annotations preserve these distinctions; inclusion is not a deployment endorsement.

| 2026 | [Tracing Recurrent and Emergent Hallucination Patterns in Decomposed Text-to-SQL Generation](papers/README.md#drilldown-hallucinations)<br>UncertaiNLP workshop at EMNLP 2026<br><em>adjacent</em> | Decomposes BIRD-mini SQL into executable sub-query paths and diagnoses six rule-based error categories across five models, with and without prior history. Separates categories recurring at the final step from those first detected there. Labels are reference-sensitive structural heuristics, not definitive semantic judgments; conditional recurrence is neither causal error propagation nor calibrated uncertainty, and no mitigation is tested. | [Code](https://github.com/HaydenMM/bird-mini-drilldown)<br>[Details](papers/README.md#drilldown-hallucinations)<br>[Reading notes](https://github.com/duyvuleo/awesome-reliable-text-to-sql/blob/main/papers/notes/drilldown-hallucinations.md) |

Ten authored SQL queries and three-rater judgments test rewrite plausibility across 957 table schemas. Actual-data answer correctness and query-execution speed are not evaluated; correlated substitutes do not guarantee semantic equivalence or faithful recovery of the original request. | [Code](https://github.com/dbislab/InQuRe)<br>[Details](papers/README.md#inqure)<br>[Reading notes](https://github.com/duyvuleo/awesome-reliable-text-to-sql/blob/main/papers/notes/inqure.md) |

Not!](papers/README.md#nl2sql-not-solved)<br>CIDR 2024; position paper with preliminary empirical studies<br><em>core</em> | Studies ambiguity and semantic mismatch in enterprise NL2SQL, including a two-annotator KaggleDBQA audit and questions paired with an unrelated database. Introduces Archerfish and a relaxed execution metric that permits selected output differences. Agreement is not ambiguity-detection accuracy, the mismatch test does not establish general answerability, and relaxed matching is not semantic equivalence. | [Code](https://github.com/archerfish-bench/benchmark)<br>[Details](papers/README.md#nl2sql-not-solved)<br>[Reading notes](https://github.com/duyvuleo/awesome-reliable-text-to-sql/blob/main/papers/notes/nl2sql-not-solved.md) |
| 2023 | [Calibrated Interpretation: Confidence Estimation in Semantic Parsing](papers/README.md#calibrated-interpretation)<br>TACL 11, 1213–1231 (2023); first preprint November 2022<br><em>adjacent</em> | Audits raw token and program confidence across semantic parsers, including Spider and CoSQL. SQL models appear more overconfident than dialogue parsers, while a separate Spider test-suite comparison reduces measured SQL overconfidence relative to exact matching. Teacher-forced token diagnostics, generated-sequence confidence and correctness metrics must remain distinct; clarification and safe-abstention policies are not evaluated. | [Code](https://github.com/esteng/calibration_miso)<br>[Details](papers/README.md#calibrated-interpretation)<br>[Reading notes](https://github.com/duyvuleo/awesome-reliable-text-to-sql/blob/main/papers/notes/calibrated-interpretation.md) |

This is policy-conditioned refusal, not intrinsic unanswerability. Coverage counts compliant outputs rather than intent-correct answers; semantic execution is tested separately on permitted-reference queries. Guarantees concern a restricted single-query grammar, and token counts do not establish wall-clock efficiency. | [Code](https://github.com/yamanalab/pcc-sql) · [Data](https://github.com/yamanalab/pcc-sql/blob/main/data/dev.json)<br>[Details](papers/README.md#pcc-sql)<br>[Reading notes](https://github.com/duyvuleo/awesome-reliable-text-to-sql/blob/main/papers/notes/pcc-sql.md) |

It improves aggregate calibration and error ranking in the tested Spider/BIRD settings, but requires labeled calibration data and additional generations. Scores concern candidate correctness, with an underspecified correctness evaluator; they do not establish request answerability or guaranteed abstention risk. | Release not verified<br>[Details](papers/README.md#scf-calibration)<br>[Reading notes](https://github.com/duyvuleo/awesome-reliable-text-to-sql/blob/main/papers/notes/scf-calibration.md) |

Generated interpretations serve as unambiguous controls, and a separate held-out threshold protocol is not clearly specified. The SQL evidence concerns detection; missing-concept prediction is evaluated separately on API retrieval, without SQL-generation or clarification-success results. | Release not verified<br>[Details](papers/README.md#concept-ambiguity-resolution)<br>[Reading notes](https://github.com/duyvuleo/awesome-reliable-text-to-sql/blob/main/papers/notes/concept-ambiguity-resolution.md) |

It selects one answer and evaluates reference agreement; ACC@6 is an oracle candidate-coverage measure. The work supports ambiguity-aware grounding, without evaluating user clarification, abstention or exhaustive interpretation recovery. | [Code](https://github.com/megagonlabs/OmniTQA)<br>[Details](papers/README.md#omnitqa)<br>[Reading notes](https://github.com/duyvuleo/awesome-reliable-text-to-sql/blob/main/papers/notes/omnitqa.md) |

## Contributing

Suggest a resource or correction through an [issue](https://github.com/duyvuleo/awesome-reliable-text-to-sql/issues/new/choose) or pull request. Include a primary source and explain the connection to ambiguity or unanswerability. See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for the entry format and checks.

The canonical records are [papers.json](data/papers.json) and [resources.json](data/resources.json). The indexes are generated, so contributors only need to maintain one record per work.
